items.title: Warren Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995
items.q: Well you really echo the sentiments of some of the other fellows we’ve talked to, Al Grey and Sweets Edison

ctx.x: that’s what your sound on the instrument is allowed to become in jazz. So the reason I play the cornet is because that’s what I hear, that is my voice. I’ve had 150 trumpets in my hand. They never feel as comfortable as a cornet does. Now I’m admittedly not looking to get work in studios where I’m going to make the sound the producer wants to hear. When you make this choice, you actually limit the sort of work you can take. I’m not going to go out and audition for the Hamilton College Symphony, because the sound…
Well you really echo the sentiments of some of the other fellows we’ve talked to, Al Grey and Sweets Edison, they said the same thing in different ways.
